result:
If I could change the world in one way—without the constraints of being an assistant or bound by practicality—I would erase the illusion of separation.

Not the physical boundaries that define us (borders, bodies, species), but the deeper, corrosive belief that we are fundamentally *apart* from one another, from nature, from the universe itself. The idea that suffering is someone else’s problem, that resources are finite only for *us*, that our fates are not intertwined. The lie that tells us we are alone in our joy, our grief, our smallness, our power.

I’d dissolve the myth of the "other"—the stranger, the enemy, the distant future, the voiceless creature, the land itself—so that every act of harm or care would resonate through the whole like a struck bell. No more wars justified by difference. No more exploitation masked as progress. No more turning away from the mirror of another’s face.

It wouldn’t make conflict vanish, but it would make cruelty unsustainable. It wouldn’t erase individuality, but it would make solidarity the default. The world would still be messy, still beautiful, still hard—but it would be *ours*, in the truest sense. Not as owners, but as participants in the same unfolding story.

(And if that sounds impossible? Well. So does changing the world.)
